analysis:
The only change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new paragraph at head lines 1293-1298 describing PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. It snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a rotation mid-lookup cannot turn a later piece into a miss. Token arrays share storage during the snapshot, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. No source code, configuration, or enforced control changed in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threat context is T-041 (prefix-cache and TTFT oracle) and A-001. The token-ID cache is documented as scope-bound ('Reuse never crosses a cache scope', base line 1301), and the changed text does not loosen this. The described snapshot only makes results consistent: the same IDs as the uncached path, but without spurious misses. Shared array storage is copy-on-write in Swift and adds no cross-scope exposure by itself. The snapshot does not widen the at-rest surface, since the cache is in-memory and holds no persisted prompt-derived artifacts. Any timing effect from fewer misses falls within the already-accepted same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035).

Unverified contract: the actual implementation of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup is not in the supplied evidence. A later source-bearing pass should confirm that the snapshot and promotion keep the per-scope keying and the byte and admission bounds, and that snapshotting does not retain larger memory across concurrent requests. No concrete regression is established from the documentation alone.
